cards.header: Which story area covers the timeline?
Which file owns the focus walk, and why does it rank stops by drawing order?

steps.title: answer
steps.text:
focus.go owns the jumps.

The walk reads the page's recorded drawing order (Runtime.Placed), so it is the order on screen, never registration order.

cards.header: Make the help modal wrap long descriptions instead of cutting them, and run the tests.

steps.title: thinking
steps.text:
The table already measures widths.
A wrap column can lay a cell over several lines.

steps.title: Read help.go
steps.text:
package ochazuke

// helpView draws the bindings help modal.

steps.title: Edit help.go
steps.text:
--- a/help.go
+++ b/help.go
@@ -212,7 +212,9 @@ func (h *helpView) row(b Binding) []string {
-	desc := ansi.Truncate(b.Description, w, "…")
+	// Wrap the description onto further lines of its row
+	// instead of cutting it with an ellipsis.
+	desc := wrap(b.Description, w)
 	return []string{b.Keys, b.Verb, desc}
